page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-24 is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the c4n family. It features 24 dedicated virtual CPUs (vCPUs) paired with 186.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a memory-to-core ratio of 7.75 GB per vCPU, placing it on the higher end of memory density for standard compute workloads.

This instance does not include local NVMe SSD storage or bundled GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage. Additionally, the instance does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures that compute resources are not shared with other tenants, providing predictable execution times.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio makes this instance suitable for memory-intensive applications that do not require massive parallel GPU acceleration or local high-speed physical disks. The hardware profile is aligned with workloads such as medium-sized databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise applications, and memory-heavy data processing pipelines.
